players.title: Players
players.description: Every account on the server, from the backend's admin routes
players.fromChatLog: The backend is not answering, so this list comes from the chat log: everyone who has spoken, newest first.
players.noneKnown: No players have spoken in chat yet.
players.protected: This account holds the backend's admin role, so kicks, timeouts and bans are refused for it.
players.partialData: Showing what the dashboard and the backend know; live status and moderation return when the game server answers.
players.noChat: This player has not said anything the dashboard has received.
players.allChat: Open the full chat log for this player
players.noHistory: No staff actions on this player yet.
players.accessExplain: The backend's own account state: separate from game bans, it decides whether the launcher may sign in at all.
players.roleTesterExplain: Unlocks the backend's tester tools for this account.

moderation.customPlaceholder: The player reads this in the launcher
moderation.kickOffline: Only an online player can be kicked
moderation.banWarning: A ban lasts until someone lifts it. The player's running game stops at its next request.

explain.kick: Closes their chat connections and signs them out. They are not banned and may come straight back.
explain.timeout: Bans them until the time runs out, then lifts it automatically.
explain.ban: Bans them until someone lifts it. They read the reason in the launcher.
explain.unban: Lifts a ban or a timeout, so they can play again.

moderation.banEverywhereHint: Each reachable controller with an account of this name bans it, each recorded and undoable on its own.
moderation.fleetDone: {done, plural, =0 {Banned on no controller} one {Banned on # controller} other {Banned on # controllers}} of {total}.{absent, plural, =0 {} one { # has no such account.} other { # have no such account.}}{missed, plural, =0 {} one { # could not be reached or refused:} other { # could not be reached or refused:}}

reports.title: Reports
reports.description: Player reports from the game, Discord and staff, oldest first
reports.emptyQueueHint: New reports from the game and Discord land here.
reports.prior: {count, plural, one {# earlier report} other {# earlier reports}}
reports.contextHint: {minutes} minutes either side of the reported moment.
reports.noContext: No chat from around that time.
reports.noRelated: No other reports against this player.
reports.noNotes: No notes yet. Notes are visible to staff only.
reports.notePlaceholder: What you checked, who you spoke to…
reports.resolutionShown: Also the reason the player reads in the launcher.

chat.title: Chat logs
chat.description: City, party, guild and direct messages as the backend relays them

filter.title: Chat filter
filter.description: {count, plural, =0 {No terms} one {# term} other {# terms}}, revision {version}
filter.deleteBody: "{pattern}" stops being filtered. The change can be undone from the revisions below.
filter.testerHint: See what the current list would do, without sending anything.
filter.samplePlaceholder: Type a message as a player would

actionHelp.flag: Delivered as sent, and marked in the log for review.
actionHelp.mask: Delivered with the matched part replaced by asterisks.
actionHelp.block: Not delivered. The sender sees it as sent.

filter.enforcement: The backend fetches this list and enforces it; the dashboard rates lines on arrival with the same rules.
filter.emptyHint: Add a term to start masking or flagging chat.

kindHelp.word: Matches the word on its own, ignoring case, spacing tricks and look-alikes such as 0 for o.
kindHelp.substring: Matches inside other words too, with the same look-alike handling.
kindHelp.regex: A JavaScript regular expression, matched case-insensitively.

filter.historyHint: Every change saves the whole list as a new revision. Restoring one makes it current again.

revisions.empty: No revisions yet: the first change records where it started from.
revisions.confirmBody: Its state becomes current, saved as a new version. Nothing newer is deleted, so this can be undone too.

staff.title: Staff
staff.description: Who can sign in to this dashboard, by Discord account
staff.addExplain: They sign in with Discord; nothing is sent to them.
staff.discordIdHint: In Discord, turn on Developer Mode, then right-click the person and Copy User ID.
staff.discordIdInvalid: A Discord id is 17 to 20 digits
staff.guildSyncHint: Members whose access came from a Discord role are re-checked at every sign-in. Changing their role here makes it manual.

roleHelp.owner: Everything, including settings and other owners
roleHelp.admin: Players' accounts, the chat filter, staff and undo

staff.historyHint: Roles and access as they were. Restoring never deletes anyone; people added since are disabled.

settings.title: Settings
settings.description: Each save is a revision you can restore below.
settings.serverNameHint: Shown on the sign-in page and in browser tabs.
settings.discordHint: Optionally let roles in your Discord server grant dashboard access, instead of adding everyone here.
settings.guildIdHint: Leave empty to admit only people on the Staff page.
settings.reasonsHint: One per line. Offered when timing out, banning or changing access.
settings.contextMinutesHint: Minutes of chat shown either side of a reported moment.
settings.retentionHint: Chat older than this is deleted every hour as new chat arrives, or now with Prune.
settings.pruned: {count, plural, =0 {Nothing to prune} one {# message deleted} other {# messages deleted}}
settings.connectionsHint: Set in the dashboard's environment, not here. Secrets are never shown.
settings.historyHint: Every save of these settings, newest first.

errors.invalid_input: Check the highlighted values and try again.
errors.conflict: That already exists, or changed while you were looking at it.
errors.reason_required: Give a reason of 3 to 400 characters.
errors.self_lockout: You cannot remove your own access.
errors.last_owner: The server needs at least one enabled owner.
errors.not_revertible: This change cannot be undone automatically.
errors.already_reverted: This change has already been undone.
errors.regex_invalid: That is not a valid regular expression.
errors.game_unavailable: The game server is not answering.
errors.game_not_configured: The dashboard is not connected to the game server ({detail} is unset).
errors.protected_account: Accounts with the backend's admin role cannot be moderated.
errors.already_banned: That player is already banned; lift the ban first.
errors.not_timed_out: That player is not timed out.
errors.unknown: Something went wrong. The server log has the details.
errors.controller_offline: {detail} is not connected. Its agent may be stopped or its host offline.
errors.game_timeout: The controller took too long to answer.
errors.forbidden_call: The agent refused a call it does not allow ({detail}).

fleet.name: Name
fleet.addExplain: You get a one-time code to start its agent with. Nothing on that host needs a port opened.
fleet.localDescription: The controller this dashboard runs on
fleet.removeBody: Its agent is disconnected and its token stops working. Chat, reports and history from it stay, labelled with its id.
fleet.pendingHint: Start the agent on that host with the pairing code. Re-pair from Actions if the code expired.
fleet.localNotConfigured: This host's admin API key is not set, so the dashboard cannot reach its game server (DASHBOARD_ADMIN_API_KEY).

pairing.title: Pair {name}
pairing.step1: On that host, write these into an env file. The two secrets come from its own secrets.env and never leave it.
pairing.step2: Then start the agent from a dainty-dashboard checkout:
pairing.after: The code works once. The agent stores the token it gets in exchange and reconnects with it from then on.
pairing.insecure: This dashboard's address is not HTTPS. Agents send their token with every request, so put the dashboard behind TLS before pairing hosts over the internet.
